column4: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is *something* true? What made it that way? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This fascination goes beyond a desire to be correct on a surface level, but to know deeply and precisely, and to be able to clearly articulate the new gained understanding.
column5: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is something true? How did it come to be so? How do we know? How are we certain? If something is true, what else is true? What is false? This interest goes beyond a surface-level desire to be right, but rather to know deeply and accurately, and to be able to articulate the newly gained understanding with clarity.

column4: While communication is common, effective and precise communication is challenging. To effectively communicate a message the author and originator must have an idea. However, the idea alone like water on a hard surface-its edges and boundaries are poorly defined, fluid, and easily moved around.
column5: Although communication is common, effective and accurate communication is challenging. To communicate a message effectively, the writer and originator must have an idea. But an idea by itself is like water on a hard surface—its edges and boundaries are not properly defined, it is fluid and easily shifts around.

column4: We use words, terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea from vaguely shaped to precisely shaped. Words give our idea a boundary, they help us distinguish and separate between what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form text, like this book, or short form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium transmits the now well-formed idea to the recipient.
column5: We use words, terms, and phrases to turn a raw idea from a vague shape into a defined form. Words give our idea a boundary; they help us distinguish and separate what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long-form text, like this book, or in short-form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium now carries that well-crafted idea to the recipient.

column4: So far, we’ve only discussed the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must receive, decode, and understand the message accurately. The transmitted and received messages should align closely.
column5: Up to this point we have only spoken of the originator and writer of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must correctly receive, decode, and understand the message. The sent and received messages should closely match.

column4: Every great human work is the by-product of effective communication. One man’s labor can only accomplish so much. To really build or perform something great, many men (speaking here generically of mankind) must labor together in a shared purpose, with a shared idea. Barring naturally occurring disasters (like a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest calamities to ever occur usually did so in significant part because of missing, broken or distorted communication. Truly life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
column5: Every great human creation is the product of effective communication. The labor of one person can only do so much. To truly build or do something great, many people (speaking broadly of humankind here) must labor together with a shared purpose and a common idea. Setting aside natural disasters (such as a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest catastrophes that have occurred were often, in large part, due to lost, broken, or distorted communication. Truly, life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).

column4: What we believe and how we communicate it has the power to build a person, a family, a community, a nation, or has the power to equally destroy them. What we believe is the foundation for our actions and is the blueprint for what we will do, who we will be, how we will exist. Because belief is expressed through action and communication, it defines the role we play in existence. Our beliefs shape not just our lives, but to a degree the lives of everyone around us.
